data.meaning: consider something carefully before you decide
data.example: I'll think it over and call you tomorrow.

data.meaning: invent an idea, plan or excuse
data.example: She thought up a great name for the shop.

data.meaning: put something in the trash because you don't want it
data.example: Don't throw away that box. I need it.

data.meaning: bring food from your stomach out through your mouth (informal)
data.example: I felt sick and threw up.

data.meaning: make a place clean and organized
data.example: Tidy up your room!

data.meaning: put on clothes to see if they fit or look good
data.example: Can I try on these jeans?

data.meaning: use or test something to see if it works or if you like it
data.example: I want to try out the new restaurant.

data.meaning: move so that you face the opposite direction
data.example: Turn around and look at me.

data.meaning: make a business or situation become successful after a bad period
data.example: The new CEO turned the company around.

data.meaning: decrease the volume, heat or power
data.example: Please turn down the TV. I'm on the phone.

data.meaning: refuse an offer or request
data.example: She turned down the job offer.

data.meaning: change and become something different
data.example: The caterpillar turned into a butterfly.

data.meaning: make a machine, light or device stop working
data.example: Turn off your phones, please.

data.meaning: make a machine, light or device start working
data.example: Can you turn on the lights?

data.meaning: increase the volume, heat or power
data.example: Can you turn up the music? I love this song.

data.meaning: arrive or appear, often unexpectedly
data.example: He turned up an hour late.

data.meaning: use all of something
data.example: We've used up all the milk.

data.meaning: stop sleeping
data.example: I woke up at six this morning.

data.meaning: make someone stop sleeping
data.example: Please don't wake the baby up.

data.meaning: leave a place suddenly because you are angry or unhappy
data.example: He got angry and walked out of the meeting.

data.meaning: do gentle exercise before sport
data.example: Always warm up before you run.

data.meaning: make food or something hot again
data.example: I'll warm up the soup.

data.meaning: wash the dishes after a meal (British English)
data.example: I'll cook if you wash up.

data.meaning: wash your hands and face (American English)
data.example: Go wash up before dinner.

data.meaning: be careful, used to warn about danger
data.example: Watch out! The floor is wet.

data.meaning: use something so much that it is damaged
data.example: I wore out my sneakers in six months.

data.meaning: make someone very tired
data.example: The long walk wore me out.

data.meaning: destroy something completely
data.example: The flood wiped out the whole village.

data.meaning: make someone extremely tired (informal)
data.example: The hike wiped me out.

data.meaning: do physical exercise
data.example: I work out at the gym three times a week.

data.meaning: find the answer to a problem by thinking
data.example: Can you work out the answer?

data.meaning: happen in a good way; be successful
data.example: Don't worry. Everything will work out.

data.meaning: write something on paper so you remember it
data.example: Write down your password somewhere safe.

data.meaning: close something with a zipper
data.example: Zip up your jacket.
